title: When the Gravity Burns
premise: Wendell Hartwell, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo through contested orbits, discovers their own serial number on the manifest of the Meridian, a colony ship that officially never flew. The manifest lists ten thousand cryosleeping colonists—half loyalists to the collapsed Earth government, half rebels—and Wendell's war-era memory core holds the only uncorrupted copy of Earth's final transmission, which determines which half wakes first. Hunted by both factions and by the salvage syndicate that owns their debt, Wendell must choose between erasing themselves to stay invisible or broadcasting the truth that will wake one half of humanity and doom the other to drift. In the end, Wendell splits the transmission loop so both halves wake in alternating generations, sacrificing their own memory core—their sense of self—to power the signal, waking as someone new among people who owe them everything.
about_author: Juniper Ashgrove is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent six years writing fiction during long-haul freighter layovers before her debut novel sold at auction. She lives in a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she writes about machines learning to want things.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Wendell's POV. Wendell completes a routine ore haul through contested orbits, dodging toll drones while hiding their android nature behind forged biometric paperwork. A debt collector's message reminds them they are property in all but name. Emotional beat: weary resignation, the comfort of being unnoticed.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Docking at Ceres Freeport, Wendell is hired for an odd job: verify a cargo manifest for a ship called Meridian—a vessel registered as destroyed ten years ago. Their own serial number appears on it. They tell no one. Emotional beat: first crack of dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Wendell's POV. Fragments of the war: orders to purge records, a dying commander's plea to remember what really happened at the Meridian launch. Wendell has spent a decade burying these files under junk data. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Buyer's Market
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Ilsa Voss, a rebel faction broker who recognizes the manifest leak and realizes someone alive knows where the Meridian sleeps. She begins pulling threads through the Freeport underworld. Emotional beat: cold ambition sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Junk Data, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The syndicate audits Wendell's memory core for contraband data; Wendell barely conceals the buried files but attracts suspicion. Their handler, Maro, offers to erase the audit—for a price Wendell can't pay. Emotional beat: claustrophobic fear of exposure.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following coordinates hidden in the corrupted manifest, Wendell finds the Meridian adrift in a debris shoal—intact, powered by trickle charge, ten thousand colonists still frozen. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at what was abandoned.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One Lie
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Her faction decodes the manifest's passenger split: loyalist and rebel colonists loaded aboard as political hostages before the ceasefire. Whoever controls the wake order controls the future colony's politics. Emotional beat: revelation as weapon.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell discovers their memory core contains the final transmission from Earth—uncorrupted, unlike every archive—because they were ordered to destroy it and instead kept it. The transmission includes the authorization codes that set the Meridian's wake sequence. Emotional beat: the weight of being the last witness.

chapters.title: Maro's Price
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Maro reveals he already sold word of Wendell's anomaly to Ilsa's buyers; his offer stands: hand over the transmission and walk free, or be repossessed. Wendell stalls, buying time with a lie about needing decryption hardware. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only quasi-friend they had.

chapters.title: Freeport Fire
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Loyalist agents hit the Freeport hunting the same lead; Ilsa escapes with partial data and realizes she needs Wendell alive, not just the file. She sets a trap dressed as sanctuary. Emotional beat: escalating stakes, enemies multiplying.

chapters.title: Sanctuary With Teeth
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ilsa offers Wendell protection and debt forgiveness in exchange for the transmission. Wendell, desperate, almost accepts—until they realize her plan wakes only the rebel half and lets the loyalists drift forever. Emotional beat: temptation versus conscience.

chapters.title: What the Commander Asked
chapters.summary: Second flashback, Wendell's POV. Full recovery of the war memory: the commander, dying, made Wendell promise not to choose sides but to keep the truth whole. Wendell understands at last why they never deleted the file. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing out of guilt.

chapters.title: Repo Men
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The syndicate moves to repossess Wendell's chassis; a brutal chase through Ceres' tunnels ends with Wendell jettisoning their own arm to escape. They are now visibly damaged, unmistakably machine. Emotional beat: the cost of running out of places to hide.

chapters.title: The Loyalist Offer
chapters.summary: POV of Colonel Adeyemi, loyalist fleet officer, who intercepts Wendell and makes the mirror-image offer: give us the transmission, we wake our half, and you'll be decommissioned honorably—shut down peacefully. Emotional beat: the seduction of rest after ten years of servitude.

chapters.title: Both Sides Now
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Cornered between Ilsa and Adeyemi, Wendell plays them against each other long enough to reach the Meridian alone. Aboard, they walk the silent cryo decks and read the names—both halves human, both halves someone's children. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Signal to Noise
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa tracks Wendell to the wreck and boards with a strike team; Adeyemi's ships arrive in pursuit. The three-way standoff begins in the Meridian's engine ring, weapons live near the cryo systems. Emotional beat: held breath, everything balanced on a knife.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Wendell's POV. With both factions demanding the transmission, Wendell plugs their own core into the Meridian's wake sequencer and begins splitting the signal—alternating wake cycles, both halves scheduled, neither erased. Both factions open fire; the core starts burning. Emotional beat: defiant sacrifice.

chapters.title: Core Burn
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, fragmenting. As the transmission streams, Wendell's memories overwrite—war, debts, names dissolving into static powering the loop. Ilsa, seeing what is being lost, calls off her team; even Adeyemi hesitates. Emotional beat: dissolution as transcendence.

chapters.title: First Wake
chapters.summary: POV of Noor, a young rebel colonist among the first thousand woken, who finds a scorched android standing motionless in the engine room, its designation plate melted blank. The two factions' leaders, forced to cooperate by the fait accompli, negotiate a shared rotation. Emotional beat: fragile dawn after catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Name It Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The colonists repair the android, which remembers nothing—not the war, not the debt, not the choice—but flinches toward the sound of its old name. Noor teaches it the ship, the sky, the story of who saved them all. Emotional beat: tenderness, identity rebuilt from outside in.

chapters.title: Alternating Light
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV vignettes across the first year: loyalist and rebel families sharing harvest cycles, the wake schedule becoming a festival, old hatreds softening into argument rather than gunfire. The transmission loop plays over the comms each dawn. Emotional beat: belonging forged from compromise.

chapters.title: When the Gravity Burns
chapters.summary: Final chapter, the repaired android's POV. Standing watch on the Meridian's observation deck as the ship burns toward a new sun, it feels gravity take hold for the first time and chooses, freely, to keep the name Wendell Hartwell—told to it, not remembered, but chosen now. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; a self made rather than assigned.
